title: Affine sections of the Fitting ideal sheaf
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\mathcal F$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module [pqf-def-coherent], let $r\in\mathbb N$, and let $\operatorname{Fit}_r(\mathcal F)\subseteq\mathcal O_S$ be the largest quasi-coherent ideal sheaf of [def-trf-fitting-ideal-sheaf]. Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq S$ be an affine open, let $n\geq0$, let $\pi:A^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal F(U)$ be a surjective $A$-linear map, and let $I_r(\pi)\subseteq A$ be its kernel-minor ideal of [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change] (the ideal generated by the $(n-r)\times(n-r)$ minors of the $(n-r)\times n$ matrices whose rows lie in $\ker\pi$, and the unit ideal when $n\leq r$). Then $\operatorname{Fit}_r(\mathcal F)(U)=I_r(\pi)$, and $\operatorname{Fit}_r(\mathcal F)|_U$ is the associated ideal sheaf $\widetilde{I_r(\pi)}\subseteq\widetilde A=\mathcal O_U$ of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]; that is, the largest-ideal construction has exactly the affine kernel-minor ideals as its affine sections.

proof.text: On every affine open U, finite_sections_of_finiteType gives finite generation of F(U). For each surjection pi, part (1) of presentationFittingIdeal_independence_baseChange identifies every summand of the presentation supremum with I_r(pi). The supremum equals this ideal: all summands lie in it, and the given presentation is a summand.

proof.text: For f in Gamma(S,U), isLocalizedModule_basicOpen identifies restriction of sections with localization; IsLocalizedModule.isBaseChange gives the canonical linear equivalence Gamma(S,U_f) tensor F(U) equiv F(U_f). Choose a finite free surjection pi onto F(U). Part (2) of presentationFittingIdeal_independence_baseChange gives a surjective base-changed presentation and its ideal is the extension of I_r(pi). Postcomposing with the linear equivalence preserves all kernel rows and hence the presentation ideal. Step 1 identifies both presentation suprema, proving principal-open compatibility.

proof.text: Package the compatible suprema as J : S.IdealSheafData using its constructor, which is the affine-ideal gluing data of lem-weil-pbc-affine-ideals-closed-subscheme. IdealSheafData.ofIdeals_ideal identifies fittingIdealSheaf with J directly. Step 1 computes its ideal on the given affine open. This is the maximality comparison already encoded in the Galois coinsertion, and requires no extra gluing or intersection assumptions.

proof.text: For an arbitrary ideal datum J, the kernel realization J.toModules is quasi-coherent, by quasi-coherence of the closed-immersion pushforward and of kernels. Its injective inclusion has image J.ideal U on affine sections, giving a linear equivalence with that ideal. Compose its inverse with sectionsTopRestrictFromSpecEquiv and apply tilde and the quasi-coherent counit to obtain tilde(J.ideal U) equiv J.toModules restricted along fromSpec. To check the inclusion equation, use injectivity of the tilde-Gamma adjunction homEquiv. The counit sends tilde.toOpen of a global section to that section; naturality of the original inclusion and IsAffineOpen.GammaSpecIso_inv_map_appIso_inv identify both sides on each element of J.ideal U. Substitute the ideal equality from step 3.
